english.title: Commissioner / staff / agent knowingly / recklessly disclose certain information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[a Commissioner, ]_
(B)_[a former Commissioner,]_
(C)_[a member of the Commissioner's staff,]_
(D)_[a former member of the Commissioner's staff,]_
(E)_[an agent of the Commissioner,]_
(F)_[ a former agent of the Commissioner,]_

knowingly or recklessly disclosed, without lawful authority, information which had been obtained by, or provided to, the Commission in the course or for the purpose of discharging

(G)_[his]_
(H)_[her]_

functions under or for the purposes of the Data Protection Act 2018 which related to an identified or identifiable individual or business and was not at the time of the disclosure and had not previously been, available to the public from other sources
english.legislation: Contrary to section 132(3) and 196(2) of the Data Protection Act 2018.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a former or current Commissioner / member of the Commissioner's staff / agent of the Commissioner
knowingly or recklessly disclosed, without lawful authority
information obtained by or provided to the Commission
in the course or for the purpose of discharging his / her functions under or for the purposes of the Data Protection Act 2018
which related to an identified / identifiable individual or business AND
was not at the time of the disclosure and had not previously been available to the public from other sources

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Prosecution only by the Commissioner or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) Section 199(1) of the Data Protection Act 2018 states that the National Police Records (Recordable Offences) Regulations 2000 (S.I. 2000/1139) has effect as if this offence was listed in the Schedule to the Regulations. Therefore offenders must be fingerprinted and photographed as well as the offence being PNC recordable.

other.penalty:
Either Way -
Summary: A fine.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
